WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the injured appellant challenging the judgment and award dated 11.07.2019 passed in MVC.No.63/2017 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge & CJM, Mandya (for short 'Tribunal').
2.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge & CJM, Mandya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. Sri

.K.L.Sreenivas, learned counsel appearing for the appellant seeks to enhance the compensation on the ground that the income and assessment of disability of the appellant requires reconsideration on the higher side.
It is submitted that the award of compensation by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on lower side.
Hence, he seeks to enhance the same appropriately by considering the evidence on record.
NC: 2026:KHC:13308 HC-KAR 4.

Per contra, Sri.S.Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that no evidence was placed before the Tribunal with regard to the income of the appellant.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has assessed one-third of the disability assessed by the doctor, since the doctor's assessment pertains only to a particular limb.
Hence, he seeks to sustain the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and seeks to dismiss the appeal.
5. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the material available on record.
6. It is not in dispute that in a road accident dated 30.01.2016, the appellant sustained injuries and as per the medical records, he suffered a segmental fracture on the left neck of femur.

The doctor,
based on the treatment provided, assessed the disability at 33% to the left lower limb, and the Tribunal has considered the said disability at NC: 2026:KHC:13308 HC-KAR 11% to the whole body.
In my considered view, the Tribunal is fully justified in assessing the disability in the said manner.
The said assessment is based on the oral and documentary evidence available on record which does not call for any interference.

sentences.text: Insofar as the income of the injured appellant is concerned, admittedly, the injured has not placed any evidence before the Tribunal with regard to his earning.
In the absence of proof of income and taking note of the notional income chart prepared by the KSLSA, this Court notionally reassess the income of the injured at Rs.9,500/- per month.
It is not in dispute that the claimant was aged about 65 years at the time of the accident; hence, the appropriate multiplier would be 7, which has been rightly considered by the Tribunal.

Having reassessed the income of the appellant/claimant, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability as under:
NC: 2026:KHC:13308 HC-KAR Rs.9,500 X 12 X 7 X 11% = Rs.87,780/-.
8.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,300/- towards medical expenses, which remains unaltered.
It is also to be noticed that the injured appellant was an inpatient for a period of 15 days and had undergone surgery.
Therefore, I am of the considered view that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is required to be reassessed by appropriately enhancing the same.

Thus, the appellant is entitled to the modified compensation as under:
 HEADS AMOUNT  (in Rs.)
Pain & suffering 40,000  Loss of amenities 30,000

Medical expenses 4,300  Loss of income during laid-up period 28,500  (Rs.9,500 X 3)
 Loss of future income due to disability 87,780
Towards food, nourishment, conveyance 25,000  and attendant charges
NC: 2026:KHC:13308 HC-KAR Thus, the appellant-claimant shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,15,580/- as against Rs.1,34,220/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.

sentences.text: 3 b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the appellant-claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,15,580/- as against Rs.1,34,220/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.

d) The Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with NC: 2026:KHC:13308 HC-KAR accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, the Tribunal shall release the entire enhanced compensation amount in favour of the appellant.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
